paper_metadata.title: Quantum walk option pricing model based on binary tree

summary: The paper proposes a theoretical discrete-time quantum-walk binomial-tree model for European call option pricing and compares it with the classical Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial tree. Using S0=100, K=100, r=0.05, T=1, N=100, sigma=0.2, the paper reports a classical option price of about 10.43, a quantum-model price of about 9.87, and a maximum difference of about 0.13; no quantum hardware or circuit-level implementation is given.

experiments.description: Simulation study comparing a classical binomial tree option-pricing model with a quantum-walk-based quantum binomial tree model for European call options across up to N=100 time steps.

algorithm.variant: discrete-time quantum walk applied to an N-step quantum binomial tree option-pricing model

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary up/down states are represented on a 2-dimensional Hilbert space per step; the N-step model uses H_N=(C^2)^{⊗N} with one qubit-like two-level system per time step.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Price a European call option under risk-neutral pricing using the quantum binomial tree formula C_N^0 = S0 Φ(τ; N, q') - K(1+r)^{-N} Φ(τ; N, q).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Risk-neutral assumption; no-arbitrage pricing via expected value under the quantum state. No penalty terms.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing with initial stock price 100, strike 100, risk-free rate 0.05, maturity 1, volatility 0.2, and up to 100 time steps.

dataset_specification.description: Single-asset stylized option-pricing setup; parameters listed in Table 1.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of classical vs quantum model price curves over nodes; reported maximum price difference and representative option prices.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute option prices at each node and compare classical and quantum price curves; report maximum difference and representative prices.

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper reports pricing agreement and convergence to Black-Scholes as N→∞, but does not claim a computational speedup.
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup is quantified; the work is a theoretical/simulation comparison.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware resources or complexity scaling are reported; the work is a theoretical quantum-walk formulation with a simulation comparison to a classical binomial tree.
limiting_factors: Comparison is against a classical binomial tree with very similar prices
Paper reports maximum price difference of about 0.13 and option prices 10.43 (classical) vs 9.87 (quantum)

notes: The paper presents a theoretical quantum-walk/binomial-tree model and a simulation comparison, but does not specify any actual quantum hardware, framework, qubit count, circuit depth, shots, or gate counts.
num_qubits inferred only at the abstract model level from H_N=(C^2)^{⊗N}, i.e., one two-level system per time step, but the paper does not map this to an implemented circuit register size.
No asymptotic speedup is characterized; the paper states the quantum model converges to Black-Scholes as N→∞ and compares prices numerically to the classical binomial tree.
The paper presents a theoretical quantum-walk/binomial-tree option-pricing model and compares its output numerically to the classical binomial tree.
It does not claim or demonstrate a computational advantage; the reported result is close agreement with the classical baseline.
